name: Theory of Computation
topics: DFA Design and Finite Automata Basics
Design a DFA that accepts strings starting with 'aba' and ending with 'bb' (or the given language) and check the given strings.
How many tuples define a finite automaton? Differentiate DFA, NFA and ε-NFA and explain ε-closure.
NFA to DFA Conversion and DFA Minimization
Convert the given NFA (or ε-NFA) to an equivalent optimised DFA.
Explain the steps of DFA minimisation and minimise the given finite automaton.
Regular Expressions and Arden's Theorem
Obtain the regular expression for the given finite automaton using Arden's theorem.
Construct an NFA for the given regular expression and convert it into a DFA with reduced states.
Pumping Lemma and Properties of Regular Languages
State the pumping lemma for regular languages and prove that {aⁿbⁿ | n ≥ 1} is not regular.
Why is a*b* regular but aⁿbⁿ not? State the properties of regular languages and regular grammar.
Grammars, Chomsky Hierarchy and Derivations
Explain the Chomsky hierarchy of grammars and languages with examples.
Explain leftmost and rightmost derivations and draw the derivation tree for id+id*id using the given grammar.
Context-Free Grammars, Ambiguity and Simplification
Construct a CFG for the given language (e.g., aⁿbⁿcᵐdᵐ or wwᴿ).
Check whether the given grammar is ambiguous; simplify the given CFG by removing null, unit and useless productions.
Normal Forms: CNF and GNF
Convert the given context-free grammar into Chomsky normal form.
What is Greibach normal form? Convert the given grammar to GNF and differentiate CNF and GNF.
Pushdown Automata
Design a PDA that accepts {aⁿb²ⁿ | n > 0} (or 0ⁿ1ⁿ) and show the instantaneous descriptions for the given string.
Define a PDA using tuples; why is a stack used as its memory?
Pumping Lemma for CFLs
Using the pumping lemma for CFLs, show that {aⁿbⁿcⁿ | n ≥ 1} (or the given language) is not context-free.
Discuss the closure properties of context-free languages.
Turing Machines and Linear Bounded Automata
Design a Turing machine that accepts {aⁿbⁿcⁿ | n ≥ 1} and show the IDs for the given string.
Give the formal definition of a Turing machine; explain linear bounded automata and unrestricted grammars; design a TM transducer for 1's complement.
Mealy and Moore Machines
Design a Moore machine that outputs A if the input ends in 101, B if it ends in 110, otherwise C.
Convert the given Moore machine to a Mealy machine (and vice versa).
Decidability, Halting Problem, PCP and P vs NP
What is the halting problem? Explain the Post correspondence problem with an example.
Explain the complexity classes P, NP, NP-complete and NP-hard with examples.
